title: How Much Do We Understand Ce L3 XANES? Ab Initio Insights into Configuration-Specific Screening at the Multiplet--Continuum Frontier
abstract: How can local multiplet signatures, collective core-hole screening, and an extended photoelectron be reconciled in Ce $L_3$ x-ray absorption near-edge spectra? Motivated by the question raised by Kvashnina [Chem. Eur. J. 30, e202400755 (2024)], we address this challenge using XSpectruplet, which couples local multiplet dynamics to continuum photoelectron propagation in self-consistent Kohn--Sham screening potentials. For Ce$^{4+}$ in CeO$_2$, our heuristic search identifies primary and secondary stationary screening states whose calculated white-line maxima lie about 7.3~eV apart after including their independently calculated total-energy difference, yet both retain the same effective local spectroscopic $4f^0$ sector. Their squared overlaps with the unrelaxed sudden reference give approximate statistical weights of 63\% and 30\%, respectively, within an independent-channel description. Their contrasting screening responses arise from collective rehybridization of occupied orbitals, rather than occupation of an additional localized $4f$ spectator, and produce contributions in both the main white-line and satellite regions. Ce$^{3+}$ in monazite CePO$_4$ provides the contrasting case of a localized $4f^1$ spectator participating explicitly in the multiplet dynamics. Independent relaxation of neutral $4f$ and white-line states gives a CeO$_2$ pre-edge--white-line gap of 10.51~eV, close to the experimental separation of approximately 10.7~eV. Its excess over the fixed-background spectral gap defines a net correction, which we transfer heuristically to CePO$_4$ without changing its local multiplet structure. This gives an estimated CePO$_4$ gap of 6.38~eV, compared with approximately 8.1~eV experimentally. Distinct spectral contributions can thus arise from collective screening without a change in the effective local configuration.
summary: This theoretical study tackles the complex interpretation of Ce $L_3$ XANES spectra by developing the XSpectruplet model to couple local multiplet physics with continuum photoelectron propagation. It demonstrates that collective screening in $	ext{CeO}_2$ can generate distinct spectral features without altering the fundamental local electronic configuration. The methodology provides a rigorous framework for understanding core-level spectroscopy in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical challenge of reconciling local multiplet signatures, collective core-hole screening effects, and extended photoelectron propagation when interpreting Ce $L_3$ XANES spectra.
main_result: For $	ext{CeO}_2$, distinct spectral contributions can arise from collective screening mechanisms without implying a change in the effective local electronic configuration. The study also provides estimates for the spectral gap in $	ext{CePO}_4$ by transferring corrections from $	ext{CeO}_2$.
method: The authors employ the XSpectruplet framework, which couples local multiplet dynamics to continuum photoelectron propagation using self-consistent Kohn-Sham screening potentials within the PAW framework.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Cerium compounds ($	ext{CeO}_2$ and $	ext{CePO}_4$), modeling the core-ionized state using the $Z+1$ equivalent-core approximation and incorporating local multiplet structure calculations.
key_observables: White-line maxima separation ($\sim 7.3 	ext{ eV}$ for $	ext{CeO}_2$ screening states), calculated spectral gaps ($	ext{CeO}_2$: $10.51 	ext{ eV}$ vs. $10.7 	ext{ eV}$ exp.), and squared overlaps ($P_1 \simeq 0.63, P_2 \simeq 0.30$) quantifying screening state contributions.
important_parameters: The calculations use $	ext{PBE}+U$ with $U_{	ext{eff}} = 5 	ext{ eV}$ applied to the $4f$ subspace.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on an independent-channel approximation, which neglects residual nonorthogonality and coupling between distinct screening channels, and involves heuristic transfer of energy corrections between different compounds.
figures_summary: The notes detail comparisons of calculated spectral gaps and the identification of primary and secondary screening states based on their calculated white-line maxima and overlap weights.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the theoretical challenge, detailing the XSpectruplet methodology for coupling local and continuum physics, presenting results for $	ext{CeO}_2$ showing collective screening effects, and finally applying the framework to $	ext{CePO}_4$ to estimate its spectral gap.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and many-body dynamics as it models the complex, non-perturbative interaction between localized electronic excitations (multiplets) and the continuum of photoelectron states, which is a core problem in advanced spectroscopy.
